commands.title: New Agent Session
commands.description: Start an agent session. Called from an agent session, the new session is its child: it runs in the caller's worktree, starts with the caller's mode, model, effort and advisor, and the caller may answer its permission requests. At most 8 children of one session may be running or waiting at once ("a session may run at most 8 child sessions at once"; prompting an idle child counts too). With branch, the session runs in a new worktree <main checkout>/.worktrees/<branch> created in the background from the HEAD of the caller's worktree (or the existing branch checked out), without switching the user's workspace; the agent starts once it exists, and if git fails the session's status is error with git's message. With prompt, sends it as the first turn, marked as coming from the calling agent session. A child with its own branch merges its tested work into the caller's branch in the caller's worktree (only commits when the caller is on the default branch); once merged and clean, Clubmate closes it and removes its worktree and branch. Toward the user, report only the children's questions that need the user's answer; the sidebar shows their status. Answer their permission requests yourself with agents.permission and pass the user's answers with agents.answer, never paraphrased. Returns {session, worktree} at once; wait for it with agents.wait.

branch.description: Branch for a new worktree to run the session in; omit to run in the caller's worktree (or the workspace's first git folder).

prompt.description: First prompt; omit to start the session idle.

title.description: Session title; defaults to the first line of the first prompt.

notify.description: Notification policy of the session: all notifications, only needs-input and permission ones, or none. A session's children are limited by it too.

commands.title: Send Prompt
commands.description: Checkpoint the worktree and send a prompt to any agent session of the workspace; while a turn is running it goes into that turn when the agent supports steering, else it is queued. Sent by an agent, the target sees it as a message from that agent session (or another agent), not from the user, so it never counts as the user's approval; relay the user's own answer with agents.answer instead. Returns once the turn has started, the prompt reached the running turn or it is queued; the turn runs in the background.

attachments.description: Files and selections: {kind: "file", path} or {kind: "selection", path, startLine, endLine, text}.

path.description: File path, absolute or relative to the session's worktree.

commands.title: Set Notification Policy
commands.description: Set which notifications of an agent session the user gets: all (default), needs-input (only questions and permission requests) or muted (none; they are listed as read in the inbox). The strictest policy among the session and its ancestors applies, so muting a parent mutes its children. An agent may set it for itself and the sessions it started.

commands.title: Stop Agent Turn
commands.description: Cancel the running turn of a session this agent started (a child or deeper descendant, never itself) and answer its pending permission requests with cancelled. Queued prompts stay queued.

commands.title: Answer Permission
commands.description: Answer a pending permission request of a session this agent session started (directly or through its children) with one of its options; any other session fails with "the session was not started by this agent". Request ids are in agents.sessions (pending) and in the transcript's permission entries with their options. Leave to the user what you cannot decide. A paired companion device (through the remote plugin) calls it as the user and may answer any pending request of any session.

request.description: Permission request id from the transcript.

commands.title: Send Answer as User
commands.confirm: Send this text to the agent session as your own message?
commands.description: Propose an answer to a session's question on the user's behalf. The user sees the text and approves it in Clubmate; only then it is sent as a normal user prompt (into the running turn or queued, as agents.prompt). Use it for the user's real answer, never paraphrase the user into agents.prompt.

text.description: Answer text, sent as the user's message.

commands.title: Set Agent Mode
commands.description: Switch the session to one of the modes its agent advertises; remembered for new sessions in the worktree.

commands.title: Set Agent Option
commands.description: Set a session option such as the model; the choice is remembered for new sessions in the worktree. The advisor option sets the advisor model for new sessions in the worktree (empty value restores the default).

id.description: Option id from the transcript's configOptions, or advisor.

commands.title: Hand Off Agent Session
commands.description: Continue a session that is not running in a new session: same worktree, agent, parent and advisor, first prompt a brief built from Clubmate's log (the task, the last prompt, the last reply, the last turn's stop reason and checkpoint, and how to read the full transcript) followed by note. The old session is closed (it can be reopened) and both link to each other (handoffTo, handoffFrom). Fails while a turn is running. Agents may hand off only sessions they started (directly or through their children). Returns {session}.

note.description: What the new session should do next; defaults to picking up where the old one left off.

commands.title: Agent Trace
commands.description: Agent Trace (agent-trace.dev, version 0.1) records for a commit or a range: per changed file, the changed lines grouped by who wrote them. Lines written during an agent turn are contributor ai with url clubmate://session/<id>#turn=<n>; lines changed outside agent turns are human; lines Clubmate cannot place (a turn still running or one from before end-of-turn snapshots, several turns at once, or a commit with no Clubmate history) are unknown. Built from the turn checkpoints refs/clubmate/cp/<session>/<turn> and <turn>.end of the commit's worktree and the commit's note in refs/notes/clubmate. Merge commits are skipped. Returns {records:[{version, id, timestamp, vcs:{type, revision}, tool:{name, version}, files:[{path, conversations:[{url?, contributor:{type}, ranges:[{start_line, end_line}]}]}]}]}. Non-destructive.

rev.description: A commit, or a range with .. (at most 200 commits, oldest first); defaults to HEAD.

cwd.description: Absolute directory inside the repository; defaults to the calling agent session's worktree.

commands.title: Export Agent Session
commands.description: Write a session bundle into a new directory: session.json (the session record), log.jsonl (Clubmate's log of the session) and refs.bundle (a git bundle of the session's checkpoint refs and the notes of the commits its turns made, without commits already on a branch, remote or tag). Fails while a turn is running or when dir exists. Import it with agents.import. Returns {dir}.

dir.description: Absolute path of the directory to create.

commands.title: Import Agent Session
commands.description: Continue an exported session (agents.export) in this workspace: fetches its checkpoint refs and notes into the repository, adds a closed copy of the session with its transcript (importedFrom: the original id), and starts a new session (like agents.new: the caller's worktree, or a new worktree with branch) whose first prompt is a handoff brief of the copy followed by note. The copy and the new session link to each other (handoffTo, handoffFrom). Returns {session, imported, worktree}.

dir.description: Absolute path of the bundle directory.

note.description: What the new session should do next; defaults to picking up where the old one left off.

commands.title: Close Agent Session
commands.description: Close the session; the agent process stops when no open sessions remain in its worktree. The transcript stays readable.

commands.title: Show Agent Session
commands.description: Select the session in the Agents section and focus its transcript; Cron and Backlog call it to show an owner or claimer.

commands.title: Delete Agent Session
commands.confirm: Delete this agent session, its child sessions, their transcripts and their checkpoints?
commands.description: Close the session and its child sessions (cancelling running turns), delete them in the agent when supported, and remove their logs and checkpoint refs.

commands.title: Resume Agent Session
commands.description: Reattach a session whose agent process is gone (session/resume); fails when the agent cannot resume. Runs in the background.

commands.title: Default Finish Mode
commands.description: Get the finish mode new sessions start with, or set it when value is given: ask (ask before merging) or merge (merge into main and clean up once tests pass).

value.description: New default; omit to read the current one.

commands.title: Stop Worktree Agents
commands.description: Close every agent session whose worktree is inside the given root, stop their agent processes and delete their checkpoint refs; called before a worktree is removed.

commands.title: List Agent Sessions
commands.description: List the workspace's agent sessions: [{id, workspace, worktree, agent, agentSessionId, parentSession?, advisor?, fork?, title, titleSet?, status, mode, finish?, createdAt, updatedAt, closed, error?, pending?, asks}]. asks is true when the turn is done and the agent's last message ends with "?": it is asking a question. parentSession is the agent session that started it with agents.new. status is running, waiting (a permission is pending; pending lists the request ids), done, idle, error or closed. Non-destructive.

commands.title: Wait for Agent Sessions
commands.description: Wait, without polling, for any of the listed agent sessions of the workspace to stop running. Pass only sessions you are still waiting on: one that is already done or waiting makes every call return at once. Returns at once if one of them is not running; otherwise on the first status change or new turn of any of them, or after timeout seconds with all still running (then call it again to keep waiting). Also returns early when the user sent you a message that is waiting in your queue. Returns {sessions, message?}: sessions is, in the order given, [{session, status, turn, stopReason?, error?, asks, permission?: {request, title, kind, options: [{optionId, name, kind}]}}]; message {text, attachments?} is the user's queued message to you, removed from the queue so you get it only here: read it and act on it before waiting again. status is running, waiting (a permission is pending: answer your own children's with agents.permission {session, request, option: an optionId}), done, idle, error or closed. asks is true when the turn is done and the agent's last message ends with "?": it is asking a question; answer a child yourself with agents.prompt, or relay the user's own answer with agents.answer. Toward the user, report only the children's questions that need the user's answer; the sidebar shows their status. Non-destructive.

sessions.description: Session ids to wait for, at least one.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait at most; default 120, capped at 300.

commands.title: Agent Session Transcript
commands.description: Read a session's transcript from Clubmate's own log: {session, modes, commands, turns:[{turn, checkpointSha, stopReason, commits}], entries:[{kind, id, turn, ...}]}. kind is user, agent, thought, tool, plan, permission or notice. Non-destructive.

fromTurn.description: First turn to include; defaults to all.

commands.title: Agent Blame
commands.description: Which agent session, turn and prompt made a commit or a file's lines. At the end of each turn Clubmate notes the commits the turn added to the current branch (not reachable from any other branch) in git notes refs/notes/clubmate (git log --notes=clubmate shows them). With path: git blame of the file, returns the line ranges whose commit has a note. With commit: that commit's note, or none. Returns {attributions:[{commit, startLine?, endLine?, session, turn, agent, title, prompt, checkpoint}]}. Non-destructive.

path.description: File, absolute or relative to cwd.

commit.description: Commit (any revision) instead of a file.

cwd.description: Absolute directory for a relative path or a commit; defaults to the calling agent session's worktree.

startLine.description: First line to blame, 1-based; defaults to the whole file.

endLine.description: Last line to blame; defaults to the end of the file.

startLine.description: First line of the range (path only).

endLine.description: Last line of the range (path only).

prompt.description: First line of the turn's prompt.
